images.caption: Dartmoor: Haytor Rocks There are two main granite rock outcrops or tors at Haytor Rocks. This is the north-eastern of the pair viewed from the top of the south-western one. The height of the one in the photo is 454 metres above sea level while the one that the photographer was standing on is just 3 metres higher. There are a couple of rock climbers visible in the shot, one at the top and one at the bottom of the crag. A 49 hectare area around the tors and nearby quarries is defined as an SSSI by virtue of the geological importance of the exposures of two principal variants (the 'Giant' and 'Blue' varieties) of the coarse, megacrystic biotite-granite of Dartmoor.
images.alt: Dartmoor: Haytor Rocks There are two main granite rock outcrops or tors at Haytor Rocks. This is the north-eastern of the pair viewed from the top of the south-western one. The height of the one in the photo is 454 metres above sea level while the one that the photographer was standing on is just 3 metres higher. There are a couple of rock climbers visible in the shot, one at the top and one at the bottom of the crag. A 49 hectare area around the tors and nearby quarries is defined as an SSSI by virtue of the geological importance of the exposures of two principal variants (the 'Giant' and 'Blue' varieties) of the coarse, megacrystic biotite-granite of Dartmoor.

images.filename: Exmouth seafront in south devon arp.jpg
images.caption: The sea front at Exmouth, South Devon, England, looking west. This town is the westward end of the Dorset and East Devon World Heritage Site, extending 95 miles (155km) to Swanage in Dorset. The Heritage Site is also called the Jurassic Coast, although Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous periods are represented.
images.alt: The sea front at Exmouth, South Devon, England, looking west. This town is the westward end of the Dorset and East Devon World Heritage Site, extending 95 miles (155km) to Swanage in Dorset. The Heritage Site is also called the Jurassic Coast, although Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous periods are represented.
images.artist: Photographed by Adrian Pingstone (on a chilly Monday before the school holidays, hence so few people) and placed in the public domain.
